label: Slack
terms_note: Automation allowed through an installed Slack app (bot token xoxb-…, OAuth scopes chat:write, channels:history, groups:history, im:history, mpim:history, im:write, reactions:write, channels:manage …). Web API rate-limit tiers per method per workspace: Tier 1 ≈1+/min, Tier 2 20+/min, Tier 3 50+/min, Tier 4 100+/min; chat.postMessage 1 message per second per channel (short bursts tolerated); HTTP 429 + Retry-After. Since 29 May 2025 NEW commercially distributed apps that are not Marketplace-approved get conversations.history / conversations.replies at 1 request per minute with limit ≤15 objects (Marketplace apps and internal customer-built apps are exempt; existing installs unaffected). Events API: acknowledge with 2xx within 3 seconds, retries at 0 / 1 / 5 min (x-slack-retry-num), 30,000 event deliveries per workspace per app per hour, verify X-Slack-Signature with the signing secret, keep ≥5 % success or the app is disabled; Socket Mode is the no-public-URL alternative.

sdks: Bolt (JS / Python / Java) and slack_sdk Python — docs.slack.dev

auth: 1. Slack app (manifest) with bot scopes → OAuth v2 install (`oauth.v2.access`) → bot token `xoxb-…` per workspace.
3. Events requests verified with the signing secret (`X-Slack-Signature`, `X-Slack-Request-Timestamp`).

endpoints.notes: Tier 3 for Marketplace / internal apps; **1 request / minute, limit ≤ 15** for new non-Marketplace commercial apps (since 2025-05-29)
ack 2xx within 3 s; retries 0 / 1 / 5 min; 30,000 events / workspace / app / hour

reference.limits: - Tiers per method per workspace: Tier 1 ≈ 1+/min, Tier 2 20+/min, Tier 3 50+/min, Tier 4 100+/min; 429 + `Retry-After`. - Events success rate must stay ≥ 5 % per hour or the app is disabled; `x-slack-no-retry: 1` opts out of retries. - Non-Marketplace history throttle: applies to apps created after 29 May 2025 that are distributed commercially; internal customer-built apps and Marketplace-approved apps are exempt.

fields.name: token
fields.help: Bot token (xoxb-…) of an installed Slack app, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer' ('You must transmit your token as a bearer token in the Authorization HTTP header', https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/). Scopes: chat:write (send, reply); channels:history, groups:history, im:history, mpim:history (list_inbound, get_thread); channels:manage, channels:write, groups:write, im:write or mpim:write (mark_read).

adapter.envelope_note: 'All Web API responses contain a JSON object, which will always contain a top-level boolean property ok that indicates success or failure'; on failure 'the error property will contain a short machine-readable error code' (https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/). ok:false answers (HTTP 200) become isError results.
adapter.rate_note: Tightest tier among the mapped methods: conversations.history / conversations.replies / conversations.mark are 'Tier 3: 50+ per minute' = 0.8/s; chat.postMessage 'will generally allow an app to post 1 message per second to a specific channel'; HTTP 429 + Retry-After (https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/rate-limits). Not modelled client-side: apps created after 2025-05-29 and distributed commercially outside the Marketplace get conversations.history / conversations.replies at '1 request per minute' with limit <= 15.

me.note: auth.test 'checks authentication and tells you who you are' (no scopes required); account carries url, team, user, team_id, user_id, bot_id.

send.note: `to` is the Slack channel argument: 'an encoded ID or channel name that represents a channel, private group, or IM channel'. `subject` and `channel` are ignored. message_id is the message `ts`. Slack allows about 1 message per second per channel.

reply.note: `thread_id` is the parent message `ts` (sent as thread_ts); `channel` is REQUIRED by Slack alongside thread_ts — without it Slack answers ok:false (isError).

get_thread.note: `thread_id` is the parent message `ts`; `channel` ('Conversation ID to fetch thread from') is REQUIRED by Slack. Slack pages by cursor (response_metadata.next_cursor), not by page number: `page` is ignored and only the first `limit` messages are returned; `id` is the message ts (Unix time with fraction). New non-Marketplace commercial apps: 1 request/minute, limit <= 15.

list_inbound.note: Lists ONE channel: `channel` ('Conversation ID to fetch history for') is REQUIRED by Slack — there is no cross-conversation inbox method. `since` is not sent (Slack's `oldest` is a Unix timestamp, not ISO-8601); Slack pages by cursor, so `page` is ignored and only the newest `limit` messages are returned. New non-Marketplace commercial apps: 1 request/minute, limit <= 15.

mark_read.note: 'Sets the read cursor in a channel': `channel` and `message_id` (the message `ts`, 'Unique identifier of message you want marked as most recently seen') are both required by Slack; `thread_id` is not used. Slack asks not to 'make calls to this method very often'.

evidence: host slack.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Let's Encrypt)
probe: 6/6 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
spec https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slackapi/slack-api-specs/master/web-api/slack_web_openapi_v2.json: 5/6 tools match (path, method, parameters, body keys, response paths)
auth_audit.notes: me: spec says "method: adapter POST /api/auth.test; spec defines GET only"; waived: Slack Web API methods accept POST as well as GET (api.slack.com/web#basics); the 2019 OpenAPI lists GET only
